ideas.title: Arabic CV & Notion Portfolio Template Bundle
ideas.description: A collection of ready‑to‑use Canva CV templates and Notion portfolio pages in Arabic and English, tailored for Egyptian freelancers in design, writing and programming.
ideas.pain: Freelancers spend too much time creating professional CVs and portfolios in Arabic and English
ideas.why_founder: The founder already creates designs in Canva and builds Notion pages, and can write the accompanying copy. The 3000 EGP budget covers template assets and a simple sales page, and 80 hours (10 h/week × 2 months) is enough to design, translate, package and market the bundle.
assumptions: Assumes Egyptian freelancers are looking for Arabic‑language templates
Assumes the founder can host and sell the bundle on a low‑cost platform (e.g., Gumroad)
Assumes no major legal or licensing issues with using Canva assets
ASSUMPTION: no pain quote cited for this idea

ideas.title: Arabic Freelance CV & Portfolio Online Course
ideas.description: A short video‑based course (5‑7 lessons) that walks freelancers through creating a professional Arabic CV and Notion portfolio step‑by‑step, with downloadable worksheets and template files.
ideas.pain: Freelancers waste time figuring out how to build a professional CV and portfolio in Arabic and English
ideas.why_founder: The founder can record screen tutorials, write scripts, and reuse existing Canva/Notion designs. Free or low‑cost course platforms keep the budget within 3000 EGP, and the content can be produced within the 80‑hour window.
assumptions: Assumes learners are comfortable with video learning
Assumes the founder can acquire a basic course‑hosting plan at low cost
ASSUMPTION: no pain quote cited for this idea

ideas.title: E‑book: The Arabic Freelancer’s Guide to CVs & Portfolios
ideas.description: A PDF guide (≈30 pages) that explains best practices, provides copy‑and‑paste text blocks, and includes links to the Canva and Notion templates, all in Arabic and English.
ideas.pain: Freelancers spend too much time drafting CV content and structuring portfolios in Arabic and English
ideas.why_founder: Writing and design skills match the creation of a polished guide. Formatting can be done with free tools, and the budget covers a cover design and minimal marketing. Production fits comfortably within the 80‑hour limit.
assumptions: Assumes the target market prefers a downloadable guide
Assumes the founder can handle PDF distribution on a free platform
ASSUMPTION: no pain quote cited for this idea

ideas.title: Simple Notion‑Powered CV Generator Web App
ideas.description: A lightweight static web page where users select a template, fill in fields (name, skills, projects), and download a ready‑to‑use PDF CV in Arabic or English, with a link to a pre‑built Notion portfolio.
ideas.pain: Freelancers lose hours building CVs from scratch in Arabic and English
ideas.why_founder: The founder can reuse existing Notion pages and Canva designs, and implement a basic form with JavaScript to populate a PDF template. Hosting on a free static site (e.g., GitHub Pages) keeps costs low, and development can be completed within the 80‑hour timeframe.
assumptions: Assumes the founder can learn a minimal amount of JavaScript for form handling
Assumes users are comfortable downloading a generated PDF
ASSUMPTION: no pain quote cited for this idea

ideas.title: Monthly Arabic Template Club (Community)
ideas.description: A paid membership (e.g., via Telegram) that delivers new Arabic CV and Notion portfolio templates each month, plus a private Q&A channel for feedback and quick design tweaks.
ideas.pain: Freelancers repeatedly spend time creating or updating CVs and portfolios in Arabic and English
ideas.why_founder: Community management aligns with the founder’s content‑creation skills. Ongoing template creation fits within the weekly 10‑hour schedule, and the modest membership fee can cover the 3000 EGP budget for tools and promotion.
assumptions: Assumes there is enough recurring interest to sustain a small membership
Assumes the founder can maintain the community with the allocated weekly hours
ASSUMPTION: no pain quote cited for this idea
